questions.stem: What mortality is quoted for paediatric acute liver failure without supportive care and/or liver transplantation?
Under the adult definition, within how many weeks of the first signs of liver disease must hepatic dysfunction start in acute liver failure?
In children with acute liver failure, encephalopathy may be absent, late or ____ even when disease is severe.
In paediatric acute liver failure, hyperacute onset means liver dysfunction lasting up to how many days?
Liver dysfunction lasting 11-30 days is which onset category of liver failure in children?
Liver dysfunction lasting over 30 days is which onset category, where jaundice is more common?
Acute liver failure in a child may be the first presentation of which two kinds of underlying disease?
In paediatric acute liver failure, what is the commonest cause in infants?
Viral hepatitis causes about ____ of fulminant hepatic failure in children of all ages.
Which of these is an infective cause of acute liver failure in children?
Which is a metabolic cause of acute liver failure in children?
Name three multisystem complications of paediatric acute liver failure.
questions.answer: Sepsis, acute renal failure, severe coagulopathy, GI bleeding, ascites, cerebral oedema, high-output cardiac failure with low SVR, hypoglycaemia, hypokalaemia, metabolic acidosis

questions.stem: What is the commonest presenting symptom of paediatric acute liver failure?
Apart from jaundice, name two common symptoms of paediatric acute liver failure.
In neonates and infants with acute liver failure, encephalopathy is often not obvious; the first signs may be jaundice and ____.
In hepatic encephalopathy grading, what does a higher grade indicate?
Lethargy and a slightly reduced conscious level are which grade of hepatic encephalopathy?
Stupor, disorientation and combativeness are which grade of hepatic encephalopathy?
No response to command but a response to pain is which grade of hepatic encephalopathy?
No response to command or pain, with extensor posturing and rigidity, is which grade of hepatic encephalopathy?
When should a child with acute liver failure be anaesthetised?
questions.answer: Emergency procedures only, due to high perioperative morbidity and mortality

questions.stem: What is the incidence of chronic liver failure in children, per live births?
Jaundice persisting beyond how many days should prompt suspicion of chronic liver failure in an infant?
What is the commonest cause of chronic liver failure in children?
When is a hepatic portoenterostomy (Kasai) done for biliary atresia?
options: After the first year of life
Within the first 8 weeks of life

questions.stem: If the Kasai procedure succeeds in biliary atresia, what is the 10-year survival?
Which metabolic condition is a cause of chronic liver failure in children?
Chronic liver failure in children may first present in which three ways?
questions.answer: Asymptomatic, as acute liver failure, or with insidious onset

questions.stem: Which of these is a skin sign of chronic liver failure in children?
Which of these is a trigger for encephalopathy in chronic liver failure?
What does the Child-Pugh score grade and predict in chronic liver failure?
questions.answer: Severity; prognosis and risk of major surgery

questions.stem: A Child-Pugh score of 5–6 points corresponds to which class and mortality?
A Child-Pugh score of 7–9 points corresponds to which class and mortality?
A Child-Pugh score of 10–15 points corresponds to which class and mortality?
Which three markers track disease progression well in chronic liver failure?
Standard liver function tests are poor markers of function and have no ____ value.
Name two causes of death in children with chronic liver failure.
questions.answer: Sepsis, massive haemorrhage, renal failure, worsening hepatic function with encephalopathy

questions.stem: In liver failure, which clotting factor does the liver NOT make?
In liver failure, the PTT and ____ are usually prolonged and are good markers of liver function.
In liver failure, platelets fall in number and function mainly from ____ sequestration.
Portal hypertension in liver failure risks massive bleeding from which varices?
Name three causes of anaemia in children with chronic liver disease.
questions.answer: Chronic disease, chronic bleeding and malnutrition

questions.stem: What should be arranged before surgery in a child with liver failure to manage bleeding risk?
questions.answer: FBC, coagulation screen, crossmatch, and enough platelets and clotting factors available

questions.stem: What do oedema and ascites indicate in paediatric liver disease?
Raised intra-abdominal pressure from ascites causes which two respiratory problems?
Children with ascites may be on the diuretic ____.
Why should extra fluid be given after drainage of ascites during liver failure surgery?
questions.answer: Ascites reaccumulates, causing hypovolaemia and hypotension

questions.stem: Name two causes of low PaO2 in children with liver failure.
questions.answer: Intrapulmonary shunts, V/Q mismatch, pleural effusions, ascites

questions.stem: Name two chest complications that are more common perioperatively in liver failure.
Which haemodynamic pattern is typical in liver failure?
Name two types of shunt seen in children with liver disease.
How is renal impairment in paediatric liver failure related to outcome?
In hepatorenal syndrome, what urinary sodium level is typically found?
Apart from hepatorenal syndrome, what two things can cause renal failure in paediatric liver failure?
Why are children with liver failure at risk of hypoglycaemia?
What two factors can affect acid-base balance in children with liver failure?
For procedures in children with liver failure, ____ asepsis is needed.
In a child with liver failure, what two findings should prompt suspicion of infection?
Which reactions does phase I hepatic drug metabolism involve?
What type of reaction does phase II hepatic drug metabolism involve?
questions.answer: Conjugation with glucuronide, sulphate, acetate, glycine or methyl groups

questions.stem: Name two drug classes whose hepatic clearance is reduced in liver failure.
Biliary obstruction reduces biliary excretion of which muscle relaxant, prolonging its block?
In liver failure with low albumin, how does the effect per dose of thiopental change?
What three factors increase the volume of distribution of drugs in liver failure?
questions.answer: Hypoalbuminaemia, ascites, sodium and water retention

questions.stem: What effect do drugs that reduce cardiac output have on hepatic drug metabolism in liver failure?
questions.answer: They impair it, by reducing hepatic blood flow

questions.stem: Name three preoperative investigations for a child with liver failure.
questions.answer: FBC, coagulation, U+E, LFTs, blood glucose, CXR, ABGs, hepatitis B serology

questions.stem: Which premedication should be used with caution in liver failure, as it may precipitate encephalopathy?
In liver failure surgery, what should you have a low threshold for?
questions.answer: Invasive monitoring (CVP, arterial line, urine output) and booking an HDU or ICU bed

questions.stem: What drug class should be given to reduce aspiration risk from ascites in liver failure?
How should the thiopentone induction dose be adjusted in paediatric liver failure?
Why should the propofol induction dose be reduced in paediatric liver failure?
Which volatile anaesthetic should be avoided in liver failure because it reduces hepatic blood flow?
Which drug class should be avoided perioperatively in paediatric liver failure?
What two precautions apply to regional anaesthesia in paediatric liver failure?
questions.answer: Check coagulation; reduce local anaesthetic doses

questions.stem: Why keep careful fluid balance, counting blood loss, insensible loss and ascites, in liver failure?
Which type of intravenous fluid should be avoided in paediatric liver failure?
What should be used to replace fluid losses and keep intravascular volume in liver failure?
In paediatric liver failure with coagulopathy, which product may be the main replacement fluid?
What urine output should be kept at during liver failure surgery?
